subject: Hyperscaler telemetry gap briefing — Redwood vs hyperscalers (next tests)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acme-ai.com>, Tom Reeves <t.reeves@octanecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Hyperscaler telemetry gap briefing — Redwood vs hyperscalers (next tests)

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Great call this morning. Quick recap while the details are fresh and a short proposed next-test plan so we can validate the observability and telemetry gaps you flagged when comparing Redwood to Octane's current hyperscaler endpoints.

Key takeaways from the call:
- You’re seeing parity on raw token quality for most prompts, but the ops/telemetry side is the blocker for your infra team (tracing, per-route cost attribution, and audit logs).
- Octane’s procurement team needs a short, timeboxed pilot and a scoped mutual action plan (MAP) before they can progress procurement.
- Target KPI for the pilot: p95 inference latency under 120ms for 1–2k rps sustained (we discussed tighter P95 targets later).

Where Redwood differentiates (ops-focused summary):
- Token-level cost breakdowns tied to routes + model-version attribution (helps your FinOps owners reconcile spend to product features).
- Built-in request-level tracing across the call path: caller → router → model variant → fallback — with trace IDs surfaced in logs.
- Automatic KV/prefix caching and batch-aware runtime that reduces per-token cost without changing prompts.
- Rollout controls (canary, A/B) and structured fallback policies that keep SLAs when higher-cost models are exhausted.

Proposed next technical tests (3 workstreams, 2-week window):
1) Latency & batching: run 1k rps synthetic workload with the same prompt mix. Measure p50/p95/p99 and compare Redwood (dedicated pool) vs Octane hyperscaler endpoints. Owner: Logan (I’ll run Redwood side) + Octane infra.
2) Tracing & observability: validate end-to-end trace IDs, per-route token cost, and event sampling (burst vs steady). Deliver: sample trace dump and per-route cost CSV. Owner: Marissa.
3) Audit/retention: show audit log exports, retention policy, and KMS key usage for private deployments. Owner: Rishi.

Attachments: I’ve included a short matrix (redwood-hyperscaler-comparison.xlsx) with proposed test harness configs and the observability fields we’ll validate. See attached Drive link.

Immediate asks for your team before we start the pilot:
- Approve the test window (proposed: Mar 16–27).
- Share a representative prompt set (10–15 prompts) and expected sequence length distribution.
- Confirm contact for procurement (I saw procurement@octanecloud on the call).

If that looks good I’ll send a formal MAP doc with dates, owners, and success criteria. Thanks — looking forward to a tight, timeboxed pilot.

Best,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hyperscaler telemetry gap briefing — Redwood vs hyperscalers (next tests)

Thanks Logan — appreciate the concise plan. A couple quick clarifications from our infra/security folks: 

1) For tracing: can you surface a trace ID in the API response headers so our side-by-side CDP ingestion can link requests? That was a hard requirement from our SREs.
2) Retention: our default is 90 days with SOC-2 evidence required for longer retention. Can you confirm export formats (NDJSON/CSV) and KMS support?

We’re okay with the proposed window — Mar 16–27 — but procurement wants to see the MAP before committing resources. Alyssa, can you send the prompt set by EOD Monday?

Tom
VP, Platform Engineering | OctaneCloud

Tom / Alyssa —

Short answers inline: 
- Trace IDs in response: yes — we can surface a request-trace-id header and correlate it to the trace exported to your tracing backend (we support OpenTelemetry exports; we’ll also include a sample trace JSON).
- Retention/export: audit logs can be exported as NDJSON or CSV. We support customer-managed KMS keys for Private deployments; hosted accounts can enable a dedicated KMS key per tenant.

Updated commitments and MAP (attached):
- Test window confirmed: Mar 16–27. Redwood will provide a test harness (k6 scripts) and a small dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool for the duration.
- Success criteria (one of): p95 <= 120ms for 1k rps with <20% variance between runs; end-to-end trace IDs present for >=99% of sampled requests; per-route token-cost breakouts match within 5% versus Redwood billing snapshots.
- Deliverables: test scripts, sample traces, per-route cost CSV, audit-export sample.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Send formal MAP and calendar invites for kick-off (today).
- Upload the obs/tracing proposal PDF to Drive (link in metadata).

Marissa / Rishi — please prepare the tracing sample and cost extraction steps for the kick-off. I’ll schedule a 30-min sync for Wed morning (Mar 17) to align runbook and roles.

Thanks,
Logan

[attachment: obs-tracing-proposal.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hyperscaler telemetry gap briefing — Redwood vs hyperscalers (next tests)

Looping with a couple of operational items before the kick-off: 

- Instrumentation checklist (for the run): 1) propagate trace-id header and map to OTLP trace id; 2) enable route-level token counters (we’ll provide a quick Prometheus exporter); 3) enable sample-preserve for first 500 requests so we can do exact per-request comparison.
- Test harness: I’ll attach the k6 script and a small python harness that converts k6 run outputs into the per-route CSVs we need for bill reconciliation. Expect those in Drive by EOD Tue.
- Escalation: if we see >30% p95 variance between runs, we’ll pause and do a deeper kernel/runtime profile — call ops and SRE on both sides.

I’ve put tentative owners in the MAP draft (Logan lead; Marissa trace owner; Rishi audit/retention). I’ll also add a short checklist for procurement to sign off (pilot scope, coverage, and contact).

Will follow up with the Drive links and the MAP doc.

Marissa
Director, Developer Experience | Redwood Inference
